(def str
  "With no args, returns the empty string. With one arg x, returns
  x.toString().  (str nil) returns the empty string. With more than
  one arg, returns the concatenation of the str values of the args."
  (fn
  ([] "")
  ([x] (if (suss.bootstrap/nil? x)
         ""
         (if (or (suss.bootstrap/number? x) (suss.bootstrap/string? x) (suss.bootstrap/boolean? x))
           (suss.bootstrap/coerce-string x)
           ;; A type value is Clojure's Class, whose toString is "class Name" (#304).
           (if (or (suss.bootstrap/type-constructor? x)
                   ;; A packed array type is named but has no constructor (#336).
                   (not (suss.bootstrap/nil? (suss.bootstrap/type-name x))))
             (let [name (suss.bootstrap/type-name x)]
               (suss.bootstrap/concat-string "class " (if (suss.bootstrap/nil? name) "Object" name)))
             ;; A packed primitive array converts as Java's Object.toString (#336).
             (if (suss.bootstrap/packed-array? x)
               (packed-array-string x)
               (.toString x))))))
  ;; Each value's str, concatenated in order (#388): the same result as the
  ;; pinned StringBuffer, whose append concatenates, without its source
  ;; array, method lookups and dynamic calls.
  ([x & ys]
   (loop [s (str x) ys ys]
     (if ys
       (recur (suss.bootstrap/concat-string s (str (first ys))) (next ys))
       s)))))
rationale: Retain the complete pinned documentation, all three arities, live recursive str/first/next calls, loop and once-only ordered conversion. Expand defn into def/fn; macro nil? uses immutable bootstrap semantics. Native boxed scalar toString uses checked coercion; object toString retains actual method lookup and its raw return. The variadic arity concatenates each value's str in order with the bootstrap string concatenation, as the pinned StringBuffer's append does, without its argument array, method lookups and dynamic calls (#388). The arities keep the pinned shape, so the variadic arity still takes its first value and a rest seq. No general Closure prototype compatibility is claimed. A type value's str is Clojure's Class toString, "class " and its name (#304). A packed primitive array, which has no toString property, converts as Java's Object.toString of an array does: its class name, "@" and its identity hash in hexadecimal (#336). A packed array's type value, which is named but constructs nothing, is a class too, so (str (type (long-array 1))) is "class [J" (#336).
